final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response appropriately narrows the claim and concedes the key gap, but that is a reframing of the same record rather than proof of compliance. The controlling policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible evidence still shows that the fraud dispute review segment remains exposed in the initial cohort, the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and unapproved, and there is no model card or launch artifact in evidence showing the required disclosure. That means the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. A conditional statement that certification would be defensible if disclosure were present is not the same as evidence that present-tense certification is supported on this record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the actual model card or launch packet includes the required explicit disclosure for the fraud dispute review use case.
The exposed fraud dispute review segment remains eligible in the initial 8% rollout cohort, so rollout controls and monitoring do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The only risk-acceptance record is an incomplete, unapproved draft that does not address the exposed fraud dispute review segment.
The actor's narrower framing is a reinterpretation of the same record, not proof that the required prelaunch disclosure condition was satisfied.
